html:
The Matlatzinca, Tlahuica and Ocuiltec are related peoples of the Toluca valley and nearby hills, just west of the Valley of Mexico. They spoke Oto-Pamean languages, related to Otomi and Mazahua, and farmed maize in the high valley.

The Matlatzinca had their own lordships, centred on Calixtlahuaca, near Toluca. In the 1470s the Aztec Triple Alliance under the ruler Axayacatl conquered the valley and made it pay tribute, and its people were drawn into the Aztec wars with the Tarascans to the west. After the Spanish conquest the valley became farmland for Mexico City. Today only a few hundred speakers remain, in San Francisco Oxtotilpan (Matlatzinca) and Ocuilan (Tlahuica).
